display.title: Yud-Tes Shevat: The Shpoler Zeide's Miracle on the Frozen River
display.summary_short: Why the Shpoler Zeide's family celebrates the 19th of Shevat: the ice broke beneath his sleigh, and his devoted gabbai gave his life in his place.
display.summary_long: A short talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, aired just before the 19th of Shevat. Uncle Yossi explains why the followers and descendants of the Shpoler Zeide, Rabbi Aryeh Leib of Shpola, hold a festive meal of thanksgiving on this day. On his way to serve as sandek at a bris, the tzaddik crossed a partly frozen river by sleigh, and the ice gave way. He called out that whoever would take his place would be promised Olam Haba, and his devoted gabbai, Yolik, gave his life to save his Rebbe. That Friday night the Shpoler Zeide waited to begin Kabbalas Shabbos until he saw Yolik arrive in Gan Eden. He then told his children and grandchildren to mark the day every year with a joyous meal, songs and good resolutions, so that he can be proud of us as we learn more Torah and do more mitzvos.
display.lesson: Thank Hashem for His miracles with joy, and live so that the tzaddikim can be proud of us.

date.note: 'Right before Yud-Tes Shevat'; aired in episode 512 (week of Parshas Yisro 5752).
